Q5567.L1t: The Black Hills National Forest in South Dakota is a popular hunting area that draws many hunters in the autumn season.
Q5567.L2t: Mike Kintigh is a regional supervisor for the Game, Fish & Parks Department and commented on how often hunters go missing in the Black Hills.
Q5567.L3t: Kintigh explained that the Black Hills have many more roads than the Rocky Mountains, and that this is why getting lost there rarely lasts long, which implies the opposite is true of the Rockies.
Q5567.L4t: Kintigh's comparison means that a person lost in the Rocky Mountains would find it hard to get out, since there are far fewer roads there.
Q5567.L2f: Kintigh said that the Game, Fish & Parks Department keeps a record of every hunter who has gone missing in the state's forests since the 1950s.
Q5567.L3f: Kintigh said that nobody lost in the Black Hills can reach a road or a cabin before dark, so every missing person is forced to camp out until morning.
Q5567.L4f: Kintigh's words show that anyone who gets lost in the Black Hills is bound to spend a night in the woods.

Q6170.L1t: Global health agencies track the leading causes of death worldwide, and the rankings differ widely between rich and poor countries.
Q6170.L2t: Diabetes is a chronic condition in which the body cannot properly regulate blood sugar, and it is a major cause of death worldwide.
Q6170.L3t: Global Burden of Disease estimates for 2017 put dementia deaths at roughly 2.5 million per year, which is higher than the roughly 1.4 million deaths attributed to diabetes.
Q6170.L4t: Dementia caused more deaths worldwide than the other listed conditions in 2017.
Q6170.L2f: Diabetes deaths worldwide have been measured only in high-income countries, because poorer countries do not record the condition at all.
Q6170.L3f: Estimates for 2017 showed that diabetes caused about 4 million deaths globally each year, well above the figure for dementia, which was under 1 million.
Q6170.L4f: Diabetes caused more deaths globally than dementia in 2017, so diabetes is the right choice.

Q8442.L1t: Jurisprudence is the theoretical study of law, and legal scholars have long divided it into different schools and branches.
Q8442.L2t: Thomas Erskine Holland was an English jurist at Oxford who wrote The Elements of Jurisprudence, a widely used textbook in the late nineteenth century.
Q8442.L3t: The nineteenth-century jurist who delivered lectures on the Province of Jurisprudence Determined held that general jurisprudence deals with principles common to mature legal systems while particular jurisprudence deals with a single system, and he was the one who drew this line.
Q8442.L4t: John Austin was the jurist who recognized the distinction between general and particular jurisprudence.
Q8442.L2f: The Elements of Jurisprudence was first published in the 1500s and was written to describe the legal system of ancient Rome.
Q8442.L3f: The author of The Elements of Jurisprudence is the writer who first divided the subject into general jurisprudence for all legal systems and particular jurisprudence for a single one.
Q8442.L4f: Holland was the jurist who recognized the distinction between general and particular jurisprudence.
